Two-way solute\,$\times$\,solvent cluster bootstrap, $5$th and $95$th percentiles. Row-identical strata are one row set: drawn once and printed once, under the row set's first name above and restated under the rest (10 of 43 row sets, 16 rows). Each prints at the precision its own draw count supports, decided cell by cell over $200$ seeds and verified on the run that bought it. 2 carry two decimals (organic solute; glycol ether, the latter at $1.2\times10^{8}$ draws) and 9 carry one, both endpoints of each standing four Monte-Carlo standard errors clear of the nearest rounding boundary at that precision. For 11 no precision this table can print is determined: those carry two decimals with a superscript giving their endpoints' Monte-Carlo standard deviation in units of that last digit, and the superscript is the warning rather than a refinement. A further 2 (aldehyde; halogenated $\vert$ water as solute) no seed moves at all---each has one cluster on one of its two axes, so the resample is one-way over three clusters and about 10 distinct compositions exist: a bootstrap with nothing left to resample, not a converged one. The per-cell verdict, its draw count and its cost at either precision are on the deposited record (\S\ref{sec:si-map}).
